text:
## Abstract

This query asked whether the GEO accessions GSE309890 and GDS309890 refer to the same record. They do not. GEO's `gds` Entrez index stores four distinct entry types — Series (GSE), Platform (GPL), Sample (GSM) and curated DataSet (GDS) — in a single database, and the accession-to-UID rule differs by type: a GSE accession maps to UID 200309890 (type prefix 2), while a GDS accession maps to UID 309890 (no prefix). Resolving both strings through `geo_resolve_accession` returned two different UIDs and two different FTP trees. Fetching UID 200309890 returned a populated Series: an *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 RNA-seq study of sertraline-driven antibiotic resistance, platform GPL24659, 6 samples, BioProject PRJNA1363958, one supplementary FPKM file of 510K. Fetching UID 309890 returned an empty record with no accession, no title, no taxon and no registered FTP directory. A count of the GDS entry type in the same index returned 4,348 curated DataSets in total, so a GDS numbered 309890 is far outside the range GEO has issued. The two accessions therefore differ in entry type, in UID, in FTP path, and in whether any record exists at all. The practical consequence: substituting one prefix for the other does not retrieve a synonym; it retrieves a different UID that may silently return a real record of another type, or nothing.

## I. Introduction

**Background.** The NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus assigns accessions by record type. GSE denotes a Series, the submitter-deposited unit of an experiment; GDS denotes a curated DataSet, a value-added record GEO staff assemble from a Series. Both are indexed in the Entrez database `gds`, which makes the prefix, not the database, the thing that distinguishes them.

**Literature Review.** The Series record GSE309890 carries no linked PubMed entry; the tool reported "No PubMed record is linked to this GEO record," typically indicating an unpublished or not-yet-indexed study. No literature was retrieved for this query.

**Knowledge Gap.** Before the query it was unresolved whether the numeric portion of a GEO accession is shared across entry types — that is, whether GSE309890 and GDS309890 are two labels for one study.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** Objective: resolve both accession strings to Entrez UIDs and attempt to retrieve each record. Expectation: if the two are the same thing, they resolve to one UID and one record; if not, they resolve to distinct UIDs with distinct or absent content.

## II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** The question is about GEO accession semantics, so it was routed entirely to GEO. Accession resolution was done first because it costs no NCBI request and exposes the UID rule directly. Record retrieval followed for each resolved UID. A count of the GDS entry type was added to test whether an accession number of 309890 is plausible for that type.

**Materials.**
- NCBI GEO, reached with `geo_resolve_accession` (arithmetic accession-to-UID mapping).
- NCBI GEO `gds` Entrez database, reached with `geo_series` (esummary) and `geo_search` (esearch).

**Procedures.**
1. `geo_resolve_accession(accessions="GSE309890 GDS309890")`.
2. `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=true)` — resolved internally to UID 200309890, esummary against db=gds.
3. `geo_series(accession="GDS309890", list_files=true)` — resolved to UID 309890, esummary against db=gds.
4. `geo_search(entry_type="gds", term="all[filter]", max_results=1)` — esearch against db=gds with the query `(all[filter]) AND "gds"[Filter]`, to obtain the total number of curated DataSets.

**Statistical Analysis.** No statistics were computed. The UIDs come from the documented rule returned by the resolver: UID = type digit + accession number padded to 8 digits, where GPL=1, GSE=2, GSM=3, and GDS takes no digit. The sample count (6) is the `sample_count` field of the Series esummary and matches the length of its `samples` array. The DataSet total (4,348) is the `total_count` field of the esearch result for the type-filtered query, not a page size. Emptiness of the GDS record is read from the esummary returning blank `accession`, `entry_type`, `title`, `summary` and `taxon` fields, together with the FTP note that the directory does not exist.

## III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Resolution and retrieval of the two accession strings.**

| Property | GSE309890 | GDS309890 |
|---|---|---|
| Entry type | GSE (Series) | GDS (curated DataSet) |
| Entrez UID (db=gds) | 200309890 | 309890 |
| UID rule applied | type digit 2 + 8-digit number | no type digit |
| esummary returned content | yes | no (all fields blank) |
| FTP directory | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/ | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/ (soft/ does not exist) |
| Supplementary files registered | 1 | 0 |

**Table 2. Content of the record that does exist (GSE309890).**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Title | Antidepressant sertraline biases resistance emergence via stress-driven rewiring of the pentose phosphate pathway: tktA enables metabolic rollback |
| Taxon | *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing |
| Platform | GPL24659 |
| Samples | 6 (3 control, 3 adaptive evolution 40 day) |
| Sample accessions | GSM9284457–GSM9284462 |
| BioProject | PRJNA1363958 |
| Date public | 2026/02/01 |
| Supplementary file | GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz, 510K, modified 2025-11-14 |
| Linked PubMed IDs | 0 |

**Table 3. Scale of the GDS entry type.**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total curated DataSets (GDS) in db=gds | 4,348 |
| Highest accession number implied by the query GDS309890 | 309,890 |
| Query translation used by NCBI | `all[filter] AND "gds"[Filter]` |

**Findings.**

GSE309890 and GDS309890 resolve to two different Entrez UIDs, 200309890 and 309890, within the same `gds` database.

GSE309890 returns a populated Series record: 6 samples on platform GPL24659, taxon *Escherichia coli* str. K-12 substr. MG1655, BioProject PRJNA1363958, one supplementary CSV file of 510K, and 0 linked PubMed IDs.

GDS309890 returns a record whose accession, entry type, title, summary, taxon, experiment type and date fields are all empty, with 0 supplementary files and an FTP soft/ directory that does not exist.

The `gds` index holds 4,348 curated DataSets in total. The number 309890 exceeds that total by roughly two orders of magnitude.

## IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** The objective is met and the hypothesis of identity is rejected. The two strings are not synonyms. They differ in entry type, and because the UID rule adds a type digit for GSE but none for GDS, the same numeric portion produces two unrelated UIDs. Only the GSE form corresponds to an existing record. The GDS form addresses a UID for which GEO returned no content, consistent with no such curated DataSet having been issued — supported by the observation that GEO has issued 4,348 GDS records in total.

**Context.** The record that does exist, GSE309890, is an RNA-seq Series comparing 3 control *E. coli* samples with 3 samples from 40-day adaptive evolution, submitted in support of a study on sertraline-associated antibiotic resistance and the pentose phosphate pathway. Its processed values are not in the Entrez record; the tool stated they exist only in the single FPKM file in the FTP supplementary directory.

**Limitations.** The empty GDS esummary is reported by the tool as an answer rather than an error, but an empty esummary cannot by itself distinguish "never issued" from "withdrawn" or "temporarily unavailable"; the total of 4,348 GDS records makes "never issued" the reading the data support, without proving it. The 4,348 count comes from a query NCBI rewrote (`query_translation` shown in Table 3), and it reflects the rewritten query. The Series record's `date_public` of 2026/02/01 indicates a future release date, so the record's content may change before that date. The absence of a linked PubMed ID means only that no link is registered in GEO; the tool explicitly noted this never means the study has no data. No expression values were downloaded, so nothing here speaks to the study's biological findings.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 is a GEO Series with content; GDS309890 is a different, empty address in the same index. When citing or fetching GEO data, the prefix must be carried verbatim, because swapping it changes the UID arithmetically and can return a real record of another type rather than an error. The next query worth running is a retrieval of the supplementary file GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz to obtain the per-gene FPKM values, or a lookup of BioProject PRJNA1363958 to list the raw sequencing runs underlying the 6 samples.

## References

[1] NCBI GEO, accession resolution (GSE309890): https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890
[2] NCBI GEO, accession resolution (GDS309890): https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GDS309890
[3] NCBI GEO FTP, Series directory: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/
[4] NCBI GEO FTP, supplementary file: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz
[5] NCBI GEO FTP, DataSet directory queried for GDS309890: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/
[6] NCBI E-utilities esummary, db=gds, id=200309890: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi
[7] NCBI E-utilities esummary, db=gds, id=309890: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi
[8] NCBI E-utilities esearch, db=gds, term=`(all[filter]) AND "gds"[Filter]`: https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esearch.fcgi
[9] NCBI GEO, example curated DataSet returned by the type count: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS6nnn/GDS6063/

## Acknowledgments

Records used here were provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus and retrieved through NCBI E-utilities. The Series GSE309890 was deposited by its submitters under BioProject PRJNA1363958.
